Anomaly details (from anomaly.json, also in your working directory):
{
    "date": "2025-10-13",
    "account_id": "frHBxlu"
}

The file data.csv in your working directory contains the daily cost data for the accounts. Investigate it with code (inspect the columns first) and determine which resource(s) caused the anomalous cost for this account on this date. A resource is identified by its name (the exact value as it appears in data.csv) and its type (the data.csv column that value comes from, written in title case with spaces instead of underscores, e.g. a value from a column named some_column has type "Some Column").

Recommended method (aim to finish in about 6-8 tool calls):
1. Inspect the columns and filter to the anomalous account. Compare the anomaly date with a baseline of the preceding normal days.
2. For EVERY categorical column (not only one), compute the cost change per value between the baseline and the anomaly date. Do this for all columns in a single tool call.
3. Decide which column is the root-cause dimension: the one whose values explain the total cost change most fully and most specifically. A change in one column often shows up indirectly in other columns, so compare the columns before choosing; do not assume a particular column.
4. The root cause can be one value or many values of that column. Include every value that materially drives the change, and nothing else.
5. Answer.

Required final answer format (JSON inside <answer></answer> tags):
{"resource": [{"name": "<resource name>", "type": "<resource type>"}]}
List every resource that is a root cause; include only root causes.

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
anom = "10/13/2025"
base = df[df['date'] < anom]
for d in [anom, '10/14/2025']:
    a = df[df['date'] == d]
    bmean = base.groupby('instance_family')['unblended_cost'].mean()
    amean = a.groupby('instance_family')['unblended_cost'].sum()
    ch = (amean.reindex(bmean.index.union(amean.index)).fillna(0) - bmean.reindex(bmean.index.union(amean.index)).fillna(0))
    print(d, "sum_anom - sum_baseline_mean = ", a['unblended_cost'].sum() - base.groupby('date')['unblended_cost'].sum().mean())
    print("top5 changes:", ch.abs().sort_values(ascending=False).head(5).to_dict())
    print("sum of all positive changes:", ch[ch>0].sum(), " sum of |noise| others (rest):", ch.drop([k for k in ch.index if abs(ch[k])>100]).abs().sum())
    print()
# rows for those families on anomaly day
fams = ['23zHd9pKgs','qtVJ1PKHrR']
sub = df[(df['date']==anom) & (df['instance_family'].isin(fams))]
print(sub.to_string())
print()
print("baseline mean num_instances for these families:")
print(base[base['instance_family'].isin(fams)].groupby('instance_family')['num_instances'].agg(['mean','max']))
print("anomaly day:")
print(sub.groupby('instance_family')['num_instances'].sum())

fams = ['23zHd9pKgs','qtVJ1PKHrR']

    x = h[h['instance_family']==f]
    print(f, "last 6 days:")
    print(x.tail(6).to_string(index=False))
    print("  typical price/ni over baseline:", x[x['date']<'10/13/2025']['price'].median(), x[x['date']<'10/13/2025']['ni'].median())

# total-check: does instance_family explain total?
anom='10/13/2025'; base=df[df['date']<anom]
b=base.groupby('instance_family')['unblended_cost'].mean(); a=df[df['date']==anom].groupby('instance_family')['unblended_cost'].sum()
ch=a.reindex(b.index.union(a.index)).fillna(0)-b.reindex(b.index.union(a.index)).fillna(0)
print("total change:", ch.sum(), "| change from the 2 families:", ch[['23zHd9pKgs','qtVJ1PKHrR']].sum(), "| rest net:", ch.drop(['23zHd9pKgs','qtVJ1PKHrR']).sum())
